page: The UpCloud PREMIUM-8xCPU-16GB is a virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 shared vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing the AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a 200 GB local SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 vector extensions, cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI, and virtualization support.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression placing the instance in the top tier. However, multi-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores, fall into the average category. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; the PassMark memory score is weak, placing in the bottom 25%, though uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths remain average at 53.66 GB/sec and 32.21 GB/sec respectively.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, this instance is suited for workloads that benefit from high single-thread execution speeds but do not require sustained, dedicated multi-core performance. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, Redis database operations, and lightweight single-threaded processing tasks. It is less suitable for memory-intensive applications or larger language model inference, as demonstrated by weak to poor performance in 7B LLM text generation benchmarks.
